articles.title: ‘Money Will Double Through Tantra’: Farmer Alleges Maulana Cheated Him of ₹1.8 Crore in Amroha
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A farmer in Uttar Pradesh's Amroha district has accused a man posing as a Maulana of cheating him out of ₹1.8 crore by promising to double his money through tantra-mantra and special rituals.

body.html:
A farmer in Uttar Pradesh's Amroha district has accused a man posing as a Maulana of cheating him out of ₹1.8 crore by promising to double his money through tantra-mantra and special rituals.

According to the complaint, the accused, identified as Jaane Alam, allegedly gained the trust of Akash Chaudhary, a resident of Sarkada Kala village in the Bachhrayun area, through small financial transactions before convincing him to make larger investments.

Akash told police that he met the accused around two years ago. During their interactions, the self-styled Maulana claimed he could multiply money through tantra-mantra and religious rituals.

To gain his confidence, the accused allegedly accepted ₹10,000 from him and later returned ₹20,000. Encouraged by the apparent returns, Akash continued investing money with him.

The complainant alleged that over the next two years, he handed over a total of ₹1.8 crore to the accused. To arrange the funds, he reportedly sold 32 bighas of agricultural land. According to him, ₹35 lakh was transferred through four bank accounts, while the remaining amount was paid in cash.

Akash alleged that the accused repeatedly promised high returns but later stopped returning the money. He further claimed that a settlement was reached around six months ago in Gajraula, under which the accused agreed to repay the entire amount on a fixed date.

However, when Akash approached him on the agreed date to recover the money, the accused allegedly misbehaved with him and threatened to kill him.

Following the incident, the farmer submitted a written complaint at Gajraula Police Station seeking legal action against the accused and recovery of his money.

Meanwhile, a video purportedly showing the accused performing a ritual in front of a box filled with currency notes has surfaced on social media. The video, which is around 1 minute and 34 seconds long, allegedly shows him conducting an aarti-like ceremony before stacks of cash.

The complainant claims that the money seen in the video is the ₹1.8 crore he had handed over to the accused.

Crime Inspector Ram Sanjeev said the accused had promised to return the money but had failed to do so. Police said the matter is under investigation and appropriate action will be taken based on the findings.

#Amroha #UttarPradesh #FraudCase #TantraMantra #ScamAlert

articles.title: Kolkata Woman Loses Job After Viral Clash With Bike Rider
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A woman from New Town, Kolkata, has reportedly been terminated from her job after a video of her verbally abusing an app-based bike rider during a dispute over a cancelled booking went viral on social media.

body.html:
A woman from New Town, Kolkata, has reportedly been terminated from her job after a video of her verbally abusing an app-based bike rider during a dispute over a cancelled booking went viral on social media.

According to reports, the rider alleged that the woman had booked rides on two different apps simultaneously and later cancelled his booking after he had already travelled more than 2 kilometres to pick her up.

Upset over the cancellation, the rider confronted her while recording the interaction on his mobile phone.

The viral video allegedly shows the woman abusing the rider and, according to reports, threatening to file a case against him despite the dispute having no connection to any allegation of assault.

The clip quickly spread across social media platforms, drawing widespread criticism and triggering a strong public reaction.

As the controversy grew, the woman's employer reportedly terminated her services, stating that her conduct could adversely affect the company's reputation.

Reports further suggest that crowds later gathered outside her residence, prompting police intervention after she sought assistance. The woman subsequently apologised for her behaviour, claiming she lost her temper because she was running late for work.

While many social media users criticised her conduct, others questioned whether the public backlash and loss of employment were proportionate consequences for an incident unrelated to her professional responsibilities.

The incident has reignited discussions around public behaviour, the treatment of gig workers, the power of viral content, online shaming, and the serious implications of making legal threats during personal disputes.

Authorities have not announced any criminal charges in connection with the incident at the time of writing.

#Kolkata #NewTown #ViralVideo #GigWorkers #SocialMedia

articles.title: BBA Graduates Arrested for Assaulting Delhi Man, Smashing Car
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Two suspects were arrested on Saturday for allegedly assaulting a Delhi man and vandalising his car after intercepting him on Sohna Road following a road rage incident, police said.

body.html:
Two suspects were arrested on Saturday for allegedly assaulting a Delhi man and vandalising his car after intercepting him on Sohna Road following a road rage incident, police said.

According to police, the accused, both 22-year-old BBA graduates and residents of Vipul World in Sector 48, were arrested within hours of the incident. A black Mahindra Scorpio-N bearing a fancy registration number, allegedly used in the crime, was also seized. Police have withheld the identities of the accused.

The victim, a 45-year-old resident of CR Park in Delhi, suffered a shoulder injury after being struck with a heavy stick and sustained multiple cuts on his face and near his eyes from shattered glass after the suspects allegedly smashed the driver's side window. A video recorded by the victim has since gone viral on social media.

Police said the victim was travelling from Sohna Road towards Udyog Vihar after personal work in Gurugram when the incident occurred between 2 pm and 2.10 pm.

According to investigators, the accused were speeding and frequently changing lanes while overtaking vehicles. They allegedly attempted to overtake the victim's car but were unable to do so due to traffic congestion.

Police said the Scorpio driver repeatedly honked at the victim, leading to a verbal altercation between the two parties. Following the argument, the accused allegedly chased the victim for nearly a kilometre before intercepting his vehicle.

Investigators alleged that the suspects then got out of their vehicle carrying a heavy stick, smashed the windows of the victim's car and assaulted him, leaving him injured.

After the accused fled, the victim alerted nearby people and contacted the police control room. An Emergency Response Vehicle (ERV) reached the spot and provided assistance.

Police said the victim had recorded a video of the incident in which the faces of the accused and the vehicle registration number were clearly visible, helping investigators identify and arrest them quickly.

Based on the victim's complaint, Gurugram Sadar Police registered an FIR under Sections 115 (voluntarily causing hurt), 281 (rash driving), 351 (criminal intimidation) and 324(4) (mischief causing damage between ₹20,000 and ₹1 lakh) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).

Further investigation is underway.

#Gurugram #RoadRage #CrimeNews #Delhi #ScorpioN

articles.title: Six Devotees Killed After Under-Construction Hanuman Temple Roof Collapses
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: At least six devotees were killed and 16 others were injured after a portion of an under-construction Hanuman temple collapsed in Maharashtra's Parbhani district on Saturday afternoon.

body.html:
At least six devotees were killed and 16 others were injured after a portion of an under-construction Hanuman temple collapsed in Maharashtra's Parbhani district on Saturday afternoon.

The incident occurred at Yashwadi village on the Manwat road, around 190 kilometres from Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, when a section of the roof of the temple's under-construction sabha mandap (assembly hall) gave way at around 3.30 pm.

According to police, a large number of devotees had gathered at the premises for worship, as Saturday is considered auspicious for devotees of Lord Hanuman.

Officials said at least six people lost their lives in the collapse, while rescue teams pulled around 25 people from the debris. Sixteen injured devotees were shifted to nearby hospitals for treatment.

Police identified five of the deceased as Santosh Gadde of Pangra, Akash Surdose of Gangakhed Road in Parbhani, Numesh Agrawal of Jintur, Suraj Kopratkar of Itali, and Shrikrishna Balbhim Gavare of Chinchwadgaon in Wadvani taluka. The identity of the sixth victim was yet to be confirmed.

Police and local administration personnel launched rescue operations immediately after the incident, with teams continuing to search the rubble to ensure that no one remained trapped.

Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis expressed grief over the loss of lives and said the injured were receiving medical treatment. In a statement, the Chief Minister's Office announced an ex gratia compensation of ₹5 lakh each for the families of those who died in the tragedy.

Authorities are continuing rescue and investigation efforts, and further details are awaited.

#Maharashtra #Parbhani #TempleCollapse #HanumanTemple

articles.title: Wife and Brother-in-Law Arrested for Allegedly Killing Newlywed Husband Over Illicit Relationship
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A 24-year-old man's wife and his younger brother were arrested in Agra on Friday for allegedly murdering him just four months after his marriage after he reportedly discovered that they were in an illicit relationship.

body.html:
A 24-year-old man's wife and his younger brother were arrested in Agra on Friday for allegedly murdering him just four months after his marriage after he reportedly discovered that they were in an illicit relationship.

Amit Kumar, who worked as a waiter at a local eatery, was found dead in a field in the Sultanpura area under the Sadar Bazar police station limits on Wednesday.

Police initially registered a case against unidentified persons under Sections 103(1) (murder), 238 (destroying evidence) and 61(2) (criminal conspiracy) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).

During the investigation, officers examined CCTV footage from the area and recovered a blood-stained stone suspected to have been used in the crime. Based on the evidence, the victim's younger brother, Bhola (20), and the victim's wife were arrested.

According to Sadar Bazar SHO Vijay Vikram Singh, the woman and her brother-in-law had been in contact through social media even before her marriage.

Deputy Commissioner of Police (City) Sayed Ali Abbas said the woman was unhappy with the marriage and that she and the deceased's younger brother allegedly conspired to kill Amit so they could be together and eventually marry.

Police alleged that the two accused attacked Amit with a stone and later strangled him with a cloth towel to ensure his death.

Investigators further claimed that after the murder, the woman staged a s***de attempt by hanging herself in an effort to mislead the police and divert suspicion.

The investigation is ongoing, and further legal proceedings are underway.

#Agra #UttarPradesh #CrimeNews #MurderCase

articles.title: Rishikesh Rafting Trip Turns Violent: Tourists and Crew Clash with Oars on Ganga Banks
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A dispute between a group of tourists and rafting staff escalated into a violent clash on the banks of the River Ganga in Rishikesh, Uttarakhand, triggering concern among visitors and locals.

body.html:
A dispute between a group of tourists and rafting staff escalated into a violent clash on the banks of the River Ganga in Rishikesh, Uttarakhand, triggering concern among visitors and locals.

According to preliminary reports, the tourists had just returned from a rafting expedition when an argument broke out with members of the rafting crew. The verbal altercation quickly turned physical, resulting in a confrontation between the two groups.

During the clash, rafting personnel allegedly used oars and paddles, normally used for adventure sports activities, as weapons. Several individuals were reportedly involved in the scuffle.

Videos of the incident have surfaced on social media, showing scenes of the confrontation and attracting widespread attention online.

The exact cause of the dispute and the details of any injuries have not yet been officially confirmed. Authorities are expected to examine the viral footage as part of their inquiry.

Further investigation is underway, and additional details are awaited.

#Rishikesh #Uttarakhand #RiverGanga #Rafting #TouristClash

articles.title: Chain Snatcher Posing as Customer Caught by Locals After Daring Daylight Theft in Hyderabad
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A chain-snatching attempt inside a cosmetic shop in broad daylight triggered panic in Hyderabad's Uppal area on Thursday, with the entire incident captured on CCTV cameras.

body.html:
A chain-snatching attempt inside a cosmetic shop in broad daylight triggered panic in Hyderabad's Uppal area on Thursday, with the entire incident captured on CCTV cameras.

According to police, the accused entered the cosmetic shop at Uppal Hanuman Sainagar posing as a customer and enquired about the price of a face wash. When the shop employee turned around to show him the product, he allegedly snatched her gold mangalsutra and attempted to flee.

The victim, Kasula Sandhya (35), a resident of Venkata Reddy Nagar in Ramanthapur, works at the cosmetic shop. The incident occurred at around 12:50 pm.

Police said the accused forcibly snatched Sandhya's gold mangalsutra, weighing approximately 37 grams, and ran away. Realising what had happened, Sandhya immediately raised an alarm and chased the suspect. A customer present in the shop also joined the pursuit.

Local residents responded swiftly, chased the accused and managed to catch him in the Uppal Mande Market area before handing him over to the Uppal police.

During the investigation, the accused was identified as Banothu Srinivas (21), a native of Sajjanayak Thanda in Yacharam village of Sadashivanagar Mandal in Kamareddy district. Police said he is currently staying in a hostel in S.R. Nagar, Hyderabad, and works for a private firm.

The stolen mangalsutra was recovered from the accused. Police registered a case, produced him before a court and he was subsequently remanded to judicial custody.

Police officials praised the alertness and prompt action of local residents, stating that their timely intervention led to the immediate apprehension of the accused and the recovery of the stolen property.

#Hyderabad #Uppal #ChainSnatching #CrimeNews #Telangana

articles.title: Bank Manager Arrested for Allegedly Killing 7-Year-Old Boy to Conceal Affair
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A seven-year-old boy, Angadveer, was allegedly murdered in Uttar Pradesh's Meerut, with police arresting a bank manager who is accused of killing the child to conceal an alleged extramarital relationship with the boy's mother.

body.html:
A seven-year-old boy, Angadveer, was allegedly murdered in Uttar Pradesh's Meerut, with police arresting a bank manager who is accused of killing the child to conceal an alleged extramarital relationship with the boy's mother.

The incident has left Ramraj village in mourning, with the victim's family devastated by the loss. Angadveer's grandmother, Baljinder Kaur, said the family had been trying to reconcile differences between her son Gursevak and daughter-in-law Gurpreet for the sake of the child.

According to the family, Gursevak has been working in Dubai for the past six months, while Angadveer was being raised primarily by his grandmother and aunt. The child had recently returned to Meerut after studying in Patiala and often asked about his parents.

Family members alleged that Gurpreet wanted a divorce, but Gursevak refused. Police said Gurpreet had developed a relationship with her neighbour, Arpit Sharma, while staying at her maternal home in Najibabad, Bijnor.

During interrogation, police said Arpit confessed that Angadveer had seen him with Gurpreet three days before the murder. Fearing that the child could reveal their relationship, he allegedly decided to kill him.

According to investigators, the accused lured Angadveer into his car on the pretext of buying chocolates and drove him to the Hastinapur forest. Police alleged that he gagged the child with his turban, slit his throat with a knife and abandoned the body near the Kali Mata Temple.

Superintendent of Police (Rural) Abhijeet Kumar said the accused was arrested within 24 hours with the help of CCTV footage. During questioning, he initially misled investigators by claiming that the body had been thrown into the Mawana canal before later revealing its actual location in the Hastinapur forest.

Police recovered the body from the spot identified by the accused and sent it for post-mortem examination.

The victim's grandmother said the family had hoped the child would grow up with the love and care of both parents, but those hopes were shattered by the tragedy. She became emotional while recalling that Angadveer often expressed his wish to have both his mother and father together.

The incident has triggered grief and anger across Ramraj village, with residents visiting the bereaved family to offer condolences. Police said the investigation is continuing and legal proceedings against the accused are underway.

#Meerut #UttarPradesh #CrimeNews #ChildMurder #BreakingNews

articles.title: Bengaluru Phone Snatching Ends in Tragedy: Suspect Collapses and Dies While Fleeing
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A mobile phone snatching suspect died after collapsing while attempting to flee in Bengaluru's Cubbonpet area on Friday. According to police, two men riding a scooter allegedly snatched a mobile phone and sped away from the scene.

body.html:
A mobile phone snatching suspect died after collapsing while attempting to flee in Bengaluru's Cubbonpet area on Friday.

According to police, two men riding a scooter allegedly snatched a mobile phone and sped away from the scene.

During the chase, a worker reportedly threw a sack at the scooter in an attempt to stop them. However, the suspects continued their escape.

Moments later, one of the suspects, identified as Junaid, suddenly collapsed on a footpath and died.

Police said Junaid had a pre-existing heart condition and is suspected to have suffered a cardiac arrest while fleeing.

The second suspect, identified as Arbaaz, has been taken into custody for questioning.

Police have launched an investigation to determine the sequence of events and ascertain the exact cause of death.

#Bengaluru #Cubbonpet #PhoneSnatching #CrimeNews #Karnataka

articles.title: Woman Alleges Husband Tied Her Up, Shaved Her Head & Forced Her to Drink Urine
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A woman from Chhattisgarh's Koriya district has alleged that her husband tied her hands and feet, shaved her head, blackened her face with soot, brutally assaulted her and forced her to drink urine in front of their children.

body.html:
A woman from Chhattisgarh's Koriya district has alleged that her husband tied her hands and feet, shaved her head, blackened her face with soot, brutally assaulted her and forced her to drink urine in front of their children.

A video allegedly showing parts of the incident has surfaced online. The victim, Tara, had married Jitendra Ghasia nearly 15 years ago after being in a relationship with him. The couple has four children.

According to the woman, years of marital discord, abuse and financial hardship forced her to live separately, where she worked as a domestic helper to support herself and her children.

She alleged that on June 14, her husband tracked her down to the residence of an acquaintance where she had been staying. After calling her outside, he allegedly began abusing her and accusing her of having relationships with other men.

The victim told police that her husband tied her hands and feet with a rope and then assaulted her. She alleged that he cut her hair, shaved her head, smeared soot and engine oil on her face, beat her and forced her to drink urine. She further claimed that he threatened to burn her alive.

According to her statement, their children were also made to participate in the humiliation. She alleged that her husband instructed the children to slap her repeatedly and that one of the children was forced to make her drink urine before the accused allegedly forced her to consume his urine.

In the viral video, the accused is reportedly heard accusing his wife of abandoning the family and living with another man. He allegedly claimed that she had previously left him and later returned.

The woman has denied the allegations and told police that her husband had long suspected her character and regularly assaulted her. She also alleged that dowry demands were made by her husband's family.

Initially, police registered an FIR under multiple provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, including Section 85 (cruelty by husband), Section 115(2) (voluntarily causing hurt), Section 296 (obscene acts and abuse) and Section 351(2) (criminal intimidation).

However, after the video surfaced and investigators reviewed the allegations in greater detail, police said additional and more serious charges were being added.

Koriya Additional Superintendent of Police Suresha Chaubey said that when the woman first approached police, she mainly reported physical assault and harassment by her husband after he consumed alcohol. Following the emergence of the video and additional facts, further legal provisions are being invoked. Police said the accused will be produced before a court and sent on remand.

The investigation is ongoing.

#Chhattisgarh #Koriya #CrimeNews #WomenSafety #BreakingNews
